evidence.field: graphic_history; reported earliest attestations; disputed interpretation
evidence.text: The article reports the earliest known 文 forms in Late Shang oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions. It describes human-shaped graphs similar to 大, with chest marks that vary or are absent; it then traces the marks’ reduction to dots or strokes and eventual disappearance in later forms. This is the author’s summary of the evidence, not an independently inspected inscription facsimile.
evidence.title: 甲骨和金文的「文」字真的和「文身」有關嗎？

evidence.text: The article reports 文 used in oracle inscriptions in personal and place names and chiefly as an honorific modifier in Shang royal names; it reports that Western Zhou bronze inscriptions use it in royal posthumous names and ancestor honorifics. The author presents Liu Yuan’s interpretation of 文邑 as 大邑 and 文 as ‘great’ as a live analysis, not a settled consensus. The article also notes that the ‘great’ account does not explain the chest mark.
evidence.title: 甲骨和金文的「文」字真的和「文身」有關嗎？

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, Shuowen Jiezi text and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: The page gives Xu Shen’s explanation 「錯畫也。象交文。凡文之屬皆从文。」. Duan Yucai’s Qing commentary interprets the phrase through intersecting patterns. This is a historical lexicographic interpretation of the seal form, not direct evidence for the Shang graph’s original referent.
evidence.kind: historical lexicographic text with later commentary
evidence.title: 說文解字「文」

gaps: The original Shang inscriptions and archaeological objects were not visually inspected; the CASE article reports their forms, readings, and uses. Exact earliest instance and its date were not independently verified against primary editions or facsimiles.
The chest mark’s referent and the graph’s earliest sense remain disputed. The sources inspected do not prove that it depicts tattooing or that 文 originally meant ‘tattoo’.

The reported early honorific uses support a proposed ‘great’ reading, but they do not establish that interpretation conclusively. The semantic path from either chest marks or ‘great’ to pattern, writing, literature, and culture is not dated by the inspected sources; do not treat a modern gloss list as chronology.

The article’s appeal to the oracle-bone phrase 文邑受禾 is reported secondarily here; the cited inscription itself was not independently checked. Taosi-sign continuity claims and the proposed derivation from 煤 were not verified.
No sound component is proposed. No independent basis was established here for the claim that 文 is the graphic original of 紋.

The provided local readings were considered only as local rows: Unihan kMandarin 文 wén and Baxter–Sagart MC mjun, OC *mə[n] (‘ornate’). The official Unihan page and Baxter–Sagart external table were not inspected in this run, so neither is emitted as externally verified evidence.
The Xiaoxuetang record page for 文 could not be accessed through the attempted URL; no Xiaoxuetang glyph image or CC0 notice was used.

Commons’ exact pages describe the selected files as modern redrawings and provide public-domain statements for the representations. No ancient artifact photograph was selected. The file pages reference Sinica and hanziyuan source material, but those underlying specific glyph records were not independently compared with each drawing here.
No small versioned local extract is recommended: no consulted source established both clear reuse terms for a repeated corpus and editorial value for a local extract.

items.period: Shang oracle-bone script style; modern vector redraw based on cited character references
items.caption: A modern redraw labeled Shang oracle style. The article describes early 文 forms as human-shaped, with chest marks varying or absent; the mark’s meaning is disputed.
items.alt: Modern vector rendering labeled 文 in Shang oracle script style.
items.selection_reason: Shows the early graph category relevant to the reported human-shaped outline and variable chest marking, while allowing the caption to qualify the disputed interpretation.
items.rights: Commons page states the SVG representation is public domain and releases rights generated in making it; this is a modern redraw, not an artifact photograph.

items.caption: A modern bronze-script-style redraw. Chest marks are discussed as variable in early forms, but whether they represent tattoos or another feature is unresolved.
items.alt: Modern vector rendering labeled 文 in bronze script style.
items.selection_reason: Pairs with the oracle-style redraw to represent the article’s reported early graphic variation and the continuing uncertainty about chest marks.

items.period: Seal-script style as transmitted in Shuowen; modern vector redraw
items.caption: A modern redraw of the Shuowen seal-script form, the form Xu Shen interprets as crossed markings; that Han explanation does not by itself establish the Shang graph’s original referent.
items.alt: Modern vector rendering labeled 文 in Shuowen seal-script style.
items.selection_reason: Shows the later lexicographic form associated with Xu Shen’s historical interpretation, distinct from claims about the Shang graph’s origin.

limitations.text: Selected glyph files are modern redraws based on external character-reference sources, not photographs or direct reproductions of dated oracle bones or bronzes; treat their script labels and shape as source descriptions pending pixel and underlying-record review.
The visual evidence does not settle whether chest marks depict tattoos, another body marking, or a different feature; the ‘great’ interpretation is a separate semantic proposal.
